content.statement: A person accepts their open invitation to a document or folder: they then have a share of it at the invitation's level, in place of any share of it they had, and the invitation goes. Without an open invitation, nothing changes.
content.why: Q7: an invitation gives no access until it is accepted, and only while it is open; accepting is what makes the share.

val acceptContract = Node.contract(accept)("AcceptContract",
  "A person accepts their open invitation to a document or folder: they then have a share of it at the invitation's level, in place of any share of it they had, and the invitation goes. Without an open invitation, nothing changes.",
  why = "Q7: an invitation gives no access until it is accepted, and only while it is open; accepting is what makes the share.",
  idea = "Invitations"
)((lib, t, p, what, result) =>
  result === lib.invitations.find(i => i.to === p && i.what === what && isOpen(i, t)).fold(lib)(i =>
    lib.copy((shares = Share(what, Grantee[Grantee.Person](p), i.level, none[BigInt]) :: sharesWithout(lib.shares, what, Grantee[Grantee.Person](p)),
      invitations = invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, p, what)))))
  .under(accessFollowsShares)
  .examples()(
    expect(withCat, now, cat, Target.Doc(plan), library.copy(shares = catViewsPlan :: library.shares),
      "Cat accepts Ann's invitation, sent a day ago: she may view the plan"),
    expect(withCat, now + 7 * day, cat, Target.Doc(plan), withCat, "eight days after it was sent the invitation has lapsed"),
    expect(withCat, now, bob, Target.Doc(plan), withCat, "Bob was not invited"),
    reject(withCat, now + 7 * day, cat, Target.Doc(plan), library.copy(shares = catViewsPlan :: library.shares),
      "a lapsed invitation is never accepted"))

content.idea:
## Invitations

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can invite a person to it, at a level,
and withdraw the invitation. An invitation gives no access until the person
accepts it; accepting it makes the share. An invitation can be accepted for 7
days after it is sent; then it lapses, and housekeeping removes it.

AccessContract.reason: Computing access from the person's grantees and the document's places is the efficient reading of Reach and Cover; the root proof shows they agree.

content.statement: A person's access to a document is worked out from their teams and the document's folders: among the shares with them or one of their teams, of the document or one of the folders around it, it is edit if one is an edit share, view if there is any, and none otherwise.
content.why: This is how the service finds the shares that matter without asking every share whether it reaches the person and covers the document: it lists who a share must be with and what it must be of, once each. That this finds exactly the shares the meaning names (Reach, Cover) is what the purpose's proof shows.

val accessContract = Node.contract(access)("AccessContract",
  "A person's access to a document is worked out from their teams and the document's folders: among the shares with them or one of their teams, of the document or one of the folders around it, it is edit if one is an edit share, view if there is any, and none otherwise.",

That this finds exactly the shares the meaning names (Reach, Cover) is what the purpose's proof shows.",
  idea = "Who can see and change what"
)((lib, p, d, result) => result === strongest(lib.shares.filter(s => granteesOf(lib, p).contains(s.withWhom) && placesOf(lib, d).contains(s.what))))
  .under(accessFollowsShares)
  .examples()(

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share reaches them and
covers it, and edit it exactly when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is.

The service answers these questions and makes these changes over HTTP, keeping
the library in memory or in a SQLite file. Versions, deny rules, expiring
shares, audit logs and outside identity providers are not part of it yet.
content.ideaSection: Who can see and change what

AccessContract.reason: As in stage 1, counting only shares in force, and nothing for a document in the trash (Q8).

content.statement: A person's access to a document not in the trash is worked out from their teams and the document's folders: among the shares in force with them or one of their teams, of the document or one of the folders around it, it is edit if one is an edit share, view if there is any, and none otherwise. A document in the trash gives no access.
content.why: This is how the service finds the shares that matter without asking every share whether it reaches the person and covers the document: it lists who a share must be with and what it must be of, once each. That this finds exactly the shares the meaning names (Reach, Cover) is what the purpose's proof shows.

val accessContract = Node.contract(access)("AccessContract",
  "A person's access to a document not in the trash is worked out from their teams and the document's folders: among the shares in force with them or one of their teams, of the document or one of the folders around it, it is edit if one is an edit share, view if there is any, and none otherwise. A document in the trash gives no access.",
  why = "This is how the service finds the shares that matter without asking every share whether it reaches the person and covers the document: it lists who a share must be with and what it must be of, once each. That this finds exactly the shares the meaning names (Reach, Cover) is what the purpose's proof shows.",
  idea = "Who can see and change what"
)((lib, t, p, d, result) => result === inTrash(lib, d).fold(none[Level],
    strongest(lib.shares.filter(s => inForce(s, t) && granteesOf(lib, p).contains(s.withWhom) && placesOf(lib, d).contains(s.what)))))
  .under(accessFollowsShares)
  .examples()(
    expect(library, now, bob, q3Report, Some(Level.View), "Bob's team may view the reports folder, which the Q3 report is in"),
    expect(library, now, ann, q3Report, Some(Level.Edit), "Ann may edit the reports folder"),
    expect(library, now, cat, plan, None, "nothing is shared with Cat"),
    expect(library.copy(shares = bobViewsPlanForAnHour :: library.shares), now, bob, plan, Some(Level.View), "Bob's share of the plan is in force"),
    expect(library.copy(shares = bobViewsPlanForAnHour :: library.shares), now + 3600, bob, plan, None, "Bob's share of the plan has ended"),

    reject(library, now, bob, plan, Some(Level.View), "nothing shares the plan with Bob or his team"),

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share in force reaches
them and covers it and the document is not in the trash, and edit it exactly
when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is. Moving a document out of a folder may take away the mover's own
access, and the last edit share of a document may be unshared.

AccessFollowsShares.reason: The purpose stays timeless: in force, open and gone are open words, proven for whatever they mean; it adds the trash, invitations and housekeeping in those words, and the least it asks of the lifetimes.

content.statement: At any moment, a person can view a document exactly when it is not in the trash and they may view it, and edit it exactly when it is not in the trash and they may edit it. Only someone who may edit a document or folder changes whom it is shared with or invited to, or moves, trashes or restores a document; a document is restored only before it is gone. An invitation gives no access, and is accepted only while it is open. Housekeeping removes only what has ended: shares no longer in force, invitations no longer open, documents gone and their shares. A share given for good stays in force, an invitation is open when it is sent, and a document not in the trash is never gone.
content.why: The idea in one statement: the shares in force decide who sees and who changes what (Q1, Q2), the trash hides a document until it is restored (Q8), an invitation is an offer, not a share (Q7), and tidying never takes away anything still in force. The last sentence is all the purpose asks of the lifetimes: without it, nothing ever being in force would meet it. Whether a share is in force, an invitation open or a document gone is left open here: Lifetimes fixes it with the clock below, and this holds whatever it says.

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share in force reaches
them and covers it and the document is not in the trash, and edit it exactly
when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is. Moving a document out of a folder may take away the mover's own
access, and the last edit share of a document may be unshared.
content.ideaSection: Who can see and change what

ClockKept.reason: Q9: the server's clock in seconds; steps take no time and a sleep may wake late, never early. The fake clock is tested against it; the computer's clock is assumed.

content.statement: The clock gives the time now, in seconds; a sleep moves it on by the time asked and by a delay it may add, never less, and nothing else moves it while a flow runs.
content.why: Q9: the server's clock, in seconds, read once per request and once per run of housekeeping. Steps take no time (the synchronous hypothesis), so a request answers at one moment. The fake clock, used in tests, is tested against this model; the computer's clock (SystemClock) is assumed to keep it.
content.definition:
val clockKept = Node.assumption(Clock.boundary)(ClockModel)("ClockKept",
  "The clock gives the time now, in seconds; a sleep moves it on by the time asked and by a delay it may add, never less, and nothing else moves it while a flow runs.",
  why = "Q9: the server's clock, in seconds, read once per request and once per run of housekeeping. Steps take no time (the synchronous hypothesis), so a request answers at one moment. The fake clock, used in tests, is tested against this model; the computer's clock (SystemClock) is assumed to keep it.",
  idea = "Time and housekeeping")
  .implementedBy(c => FakeClock(c), _.state)
model:
now = do
    let c ← get
    pure c.now

sleep = fun (seconds : Int) => do
    modify (fun c => (ClockState.mk ((c.now + (max seconds 0)) + (max (Option.getD (List.head? c.delays) 0) 0)) (List.drop (Int.toNat 1) c.delays)))
content.idea:
## Time and housekeeping

Time is the server's clock, in seconds, read once for each request: a request
is answered at one moment. Housekeeping runs every minute, one at a time with
the requests; it removes shares that have ended, invitations that have lapsed,
and documents gone from the trash. Nothing waits for it: it only tidies.

ClockNeverGoesBack.reason: Q9: the server's clock never goes back; a clock set back by hand would break it, and it is stated so.

content.statement: Time never goes back between the service's events: each wait is of no time or more.
content.why: Q9: the server's clock never goes back. A clock set back (by hand, or by a time server) would break this; the server reads the clock once per request, so it would answer as if earlier.

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share reaches them and
covers it, and edit it exactly when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is.

The service answers these questions and makes these changes over HTTP, keeping
the library in memory or in a SQLite file. Versions, deny rules, expiring
shares, audit logs and outside identity providers are not part of it yet.
content.ideaSection: Who can see and change what

The demo library (Demo.scala) is the data the examples are decided on.

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share in force reaches
them and covers it and the document is not in the trash, and edit it exactly
when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is. Moving a document out of a folder may take away the mover's own
access, and the last edit share of a document may be unshared.

EndedStaysEnded.reason: Stability in time: ended, lapsed and gone are one-way, given ClockNeverGoesBack.

content.statement: What has ended stays ended: time in the service never goes back, so a share once ended, an invitation once lapsed and a document once gone stay so for the rest of the run.
content.why: Stability in time: these facts change only one way, which is what lets the service cache them and housekeeping remove them for good. It rests on the clock never going back (ClockNeverGoesBack).

sources.formula:
forall((pre: Term[List[Event]], post: Term[List[Event]]) => (events === pre ++ post) ==> (after(pre).now <= after(events).now)) &&
    forall((t: Term[BigInt], u: Term[BigInt]) => (t <= u) ==>
      (forall((s: Term[Share]) => !inForce(s, t) ==> !inForce(s, u)) &&
       forall((i: Term[Invitation]) => !isOpen(i, t) ==> !isOpen(i, u)) &&
       forall((doc: Term[Document]) => gone(doc, t) ==> gone(doc, u))))

vocabulary: events: what has happened to the service since it started, in order: the requests answered, the runs of housekeeping, and time passing
gone: whether a document is gone at a moment: past restoring, purged by the next housekeeping
inForce: whether a share is in force at a moment: it gives access then
isOpen: whether an invitation is open at a moment: it can be accepted then
mayEdit: whether a person may edit a document or folder at a moment
startedAt: when the service started, in seconds
uses: case class PersonId(name: String)
case class DocumentId(name: String)
case class FolderId(name: String)
enum Target: case Doc(id: DocumentId), case InFolder(id: FolderId)
case class TeamId(name: String)
enum Grantee: case Person(id: PersonId), case Team(id: TeamId)
enum Level: case View, case Edit

enum Request: case Access(person: PersonId, doc: DocumentId), case Share(by: PersonId, what: Target, withWhom: Grantee, level: Level, until: Option[BigInt]), case Unshare(by: PersonId, what: Target, withWhom: Grantee), case Move(by: PersonId, doc: DocumentId, into: Option[FolderId]), case Invite(by: PersonId, to: PersonId, what: Target, level: Level), case Accept(person: PersonId, what: Target), case Withdraw(by: PersonId, to: PersonId, what: Target), case Trash(by: PersonId, doc: DocumentId), case Restore(by: PersonId, doc: DocumentId)
enum Event: case Asked(request: Request), case Housekept, case Waited(seconds: BigInt)
case class Document(id: DocumentId, title: String, folders: List[FolderId], trashed: Option[BigInt])
case class Folder(id: FolderId, name: String, folders: List[FolderId])
case class Team(id: TeamId, members: List[PersonId])
case class Share(what: Target, withWhom: Grantee, level: Level, until: Option[BigInt])
case class Invitation(to: PersonId, what: Target, level: Level, by: PersonId, sent: BigInt)
case class Library(documents: List[Document], folders: List[Folder], teams: List[Team], shares: List[Share], invitations: List[Invitation])
case class Moment(library: Library, now: BigInt, tidied: BigInt)

Run.after = (es: Term[List[Event]]) =>
    es.foldLeft(Moment(Library(Nil, Nil, Nil, Nil, Nil), startedAt, startedAt): Term[Moment])((m, e) => step(m, e))

Run.step = (m: Term[Moment], e: Term[Event]) =>
    e.on[Event.Asked](r => m.copy((library = answered(m.library, m.now, r))))
      .on[Event.Housekept.type](m.copy((library = Housekeeping.tidyCode(m.library, m.now), tidied = m.now)))
      .on[Event.Waited](d => m.copy((now = m.now + d)))

Run.answered = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], r: Term[Request]) =>
    r.on[Request.Access]((_, _) => lib)
      .on[Request.Share]((by, what, withWhom, level, until) => Sharing.shareCode(lib, t, by, Share(what, withWhom, level, until)))
      .on[Request.Unshare]((by, what, withWhom) => Sharing.unshareCode(lib, t, by, what, withWhom))
      .on[Request.Move]((by, d, into) => Sharing.moveCode(lib, t, by, d, into))
      .on[Request.Invite]((by, to, what, level) => Invitations.inviteCode(lib, t, by, to, what, level))
      .on[Request.Accept]((p, what) => Invitations.acceptCode(lib, t, p, what))
      .on[Request.Withdraw]((by, to, what) => Invitations.withdrawCode(lib, t, by, to, what))
      .on[Request.Trash]((by, d) => Trash.trashCode(lib, t, by, d))
      .on[Request.Restore]((by, d) => Trash.restoreCode(lib, t, by, d))

Sharing.shareCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], s: Term[Share]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, s.what).fold(lib.copy((shares = s :: sharesWithout(lib.shares, s.what, s.withWhom))), lib)

Sharing.sharesWithout = (ss: Term[List[Share]], what: Term[Target], withWhom: Term[Grantee]) =>
    ss.filterNot(s => s.what === what && s.withWhom === withWhom)

Sharing.unshareCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target], withWhom: Term[Grantee]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((shares = sharesWithout(lib.shares, what, withWhom))), lib)

Sharing.moveCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    val placed = foldersAt(lib, into)
    mayMove(lib, t, by, d, into).fold(lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d).fold(doc.copy((folders = placed)), doc)))), lib)

Sharing.mayMove = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)) &&
      into.fold(True)(f => lib.folders.exists(folder => folder.id === f) && mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.InFolder](f)))

Sharing.foldersAt = (lib: Term[Library], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    into.fold(List.empty[FolderId])(f => lib.folders.find(folder => folder.id === f).fold(List.empty[FolderId])(folder => folder.folders ++ List(f)))

Invitations.inviteCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target], level: Term[Level]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((invitations = Invitation(to, what, level, by, t) :: invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, to, what))), lib)

Invitations.invitationsWithout = (is: Term[List[Invitation]], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    is.filterNot(i => i.to === to && i.what === what)

Invitations.acceptCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], p: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    lib.invitations.find(i => i.to === p && i.what === what && isOpen(i, t)).fold(lib)(i =>
      lib.copy((shares = Share(what, Grantee[Grantee.Person](p), i.level, none[BigInt]) :: sharesWithout(lib.shares, what, Grantee[Grantee.Person](p)),
        invitations = invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, p, what))))

Invitations.withdrawCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((invitations = invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, to, what))), lib)

Trash.trashCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)).fold(
      lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d && !doc.trashed.isDefined).fold(doc.copy((trashed = some(t))), doc)))), lib)

Trash.restoreCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayRestore(lib, t, by, d).fold(
      lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d && !gone(doc, t)).fold(doc.copy((trashed = none[BigInt])), doc)))), lib)

Trash.mayRestore = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)) && lib.documents.exists(doc => doc.id === d && doc.trashed.isDefined && !gone(doc, t))

Housekeeping.tidyCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt]) =>
    lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.filterNot(doc => gone(doc, t)),
      shares = lib.shares.filter(s => inForce(s, t) && !ofGone(lib, t, s)),
      invitations = lib.invitations.filter(i => isOpen(i, t))))

Housekeeping.ofGone = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], s: Term[Share]) =>
    lib.documents.exists(doc => gone(doc, t) && s.what === Target[Target.Doc](doc.id))

  why = "Stability in time: these facts change only one way, which is what lets the service cache them and housekeeping remove them for good. It rests on the clock never going back (ClockNeverGoesBack).",
  idea = "Time and housekeeping"
)(forall((pre: Term[List[Event]], post: Term[List[Event]]) => (events === pre ++ post) ==> (after(pre).now <= after(events).now)) &&
  forall((t: Term[BigInt], u: Term[BigInt]) => (t <= u) ==>
    (forall((s: Term[Share]) => !inForce(s, t) ==> !inForce(s, u)) &&
     forall((i: Term[Invitation]) => !isOpen(i, t) ==> !isOpen(i, u)) &&
     forall((doc: Term[Document]) => gone(doc, t) ==> gone(doc, u)))))
  .under(accessFollowsShares)

ExpiredSharesGiveNoAccess.reason: Q6: access stops at the end time before any job runs; proven of the access code.

forall((lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], p: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    Sharing.accessCode(lib, t, p, d) ===
      Sharing.accessCode(lib.copy((shares = lib.shares.filter(s => s.until.fold(True)(end => t < end)))), t, p, d))

vocabulary: inForce: whether a share is in force at a moment: it gives access then
inTrash: whether a document is in the trash
uses: case class DocumentId(name: String)
case class FolderId(name: String)
case class Document(id: DocumentId, title: String, folders: List[FolderId], trashed: Option[BigInt])
case class Folder(id: FolderId, name: String, folders: List[FolderId])
case class TeamId(name: String)
case class PersonId(name: String)
case class Team(id: TeamId, members: List[PersonId])
enum Target: case Doc(id: DocumentId), case InFolder(id: FolderId)
enum Grantee: case Person(id: PersonId), case Team(id: TeamId)
enum Level: case View, case Edit
case class Share(what: Target, withWhom: Grantee, level: Level, until: Option[BigInt])
case class Invitation(to: PersonId, what: Target, level: Level, by: PersonId, sent: BigInt)
case class Library(documents: List[Document], folders: List[Folder], teams: List[Team], shares: List[Share], invitations: List[Invitation])

Sharing.accessCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], p: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    val (grantees, places) = (granteesOf(lib, p), placesOf(lib, d))
    inTrash(lib, d).fold(none[Level], strongest(lib.shares.filter(s => inForce(s, t) && grantees.contains(s.withWhom) && places.contains(s.what))))

Sharing.strongest = (ss: Term[List[Share]]) =>
    ss.exists(s => s.level === Level.Edit).fold(some(Level.Edit: Term[Level]), ss.isEmpty.fold(none[Level], some(Level.View: Term[Level])))

Sharing.granteesOf = (lib: Term[Library], p: Term[PersonId]) =>
    Grantee[Grantee.Person](p) :: lib.teams.filter(t => t.members.contains(p)).map(t => Grantee[Grantee.Team](t.id))

Sharing.placesOf = (lib: Term[Library], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    Target[Target.Doc](d) :: lib.documents.filter(doc => doc.id === d).flatMap(doc => doc.folders.map(f => Target[Target.InFolder](f)))

    r.on[Request.Access]((_, _) => lib)

      .on[Request.Unshare]((by, what, withWhom) => Sharing.unshare(lib, by, what, withWhom))

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share reaches them and
covers it, and edit it exactly when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is.

The service answers these questions and makes these changes over HTTP, keeping
the library in memory or in a SQLite file. Versions, deny rules, expiring
shares, audit logs and outside identity providers are not part of it yet.

SharingHttp.afterRequest = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], r: Term[Request]) =>
    r.on[Request.Access]((_, _) => lib)
      .on[Request.Share]((by, what, withWhom, level, until) => Sharing.share(lib, t, by, Share(what, withWhom, level, until)))
      .on[Request.Unshare]((by, what, withWhom) => Sharing.unshare(lib, t, by, what, withWhom))
      .on[Request.Move]((by, d, into) => Sharing.move(lib, t, by, d, into))
      .on[Request.Invite]((by, to, what, level) => Invitations.invite(lib, t, by, to, what, level))
      .on[Request.Accept]((p, what) => Invitations.accept(lib, t, p, what))
      .on[Request.Withdraw]((by, to, what) => Invitations.withdraw(lib, t, by, to, what))
      .on[Request.Trash]((by, d) => Trash.trash(lib, t, by, d))
      .on[Request.Restore]((by, d) => Trash.restore(lib, t, by, d))

SharingHttp.answerTo = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], r: Term[Request]) =>
    r.on[Request.Access]((p, d) => Answer[Answer.Access](Sharing.access(lib, t, p, d)))
      .on[Request.Share]((by, what, _, _, _) => allowedWhen(mayEdit(lib, t, by, what)))
      .on[Request.Unshare]((by, what, _) => allowedWhen(mayEdit(lib, t, by, what)))
      .on[Request.Move]((by, d, into) => allowedWhen(Sharing.mayMove(lib, t, by, d, into)))
      .on[Request.Invite]((by, _, what, _) => allowedWhen(mayEdit(lib, t, by, what)))
      .on[Request.Accept]((p, what) => allowedWhen(lib.invitations.exists(i => i.to === p && i.what === what && isOpen(i, t))))
      .on[Request.Withdraw]((by, _, what) => allowedWhen(mayEdit(lib, t, by, what)))
      .on[Request.Trash]((by, d) => allowedWhen(mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d))))
      .on[Request.Restore]((by, d) => allowedWhen(Trash.mayRestore(lib, t, by, d)))

Sharing.mayMove = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)) &&
      into.fold(True)(f => lib.folders.exists(folder => folder.id === f) && mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.InFolder](f)))

Trash.mayRestore = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)) && lib.documents.exists(doc => doc.id === d && doc.trashed.isDefined && !gone(doc, t))
content.definition:
val handleContract = Node.contract(handle)("HandleContract",
  "A request is answered at the time the clock gives, from the library the store holds, and leaves the store holding the library it leads to: a question is answered with the person's access and changes nothing; a change is made as its operation makes it, and answered done when it may be made and refused otherwise. Handling does not move the clock.",
  why = "This is the service as a client sees it, in the store's and the clock's terms (LibraryKept, ClockKept). What the answers and changes are is the operations' (their contracts); what this adds is that each request reads the library the last one left and the clock once, and leaves the library it leads to, so a client's next request sees its change.",
  idea = "Serving"
)((r, result, before, after) =>
  after(LibraryModel) === afterRequest(before(LibraryModel), before(ClockModel).now, r) && after(ClockModel) === before(ClockModel) &&
    result === answerTo(before(LibraryModel), before(ClockModel).now, r))
  .under(accessFollowsShares)
  .examples()(
    expect(Request.Access(bob, q3Report), at(library), Answer.Access(Some(Level.View)), at(library),
      "Bob's team may view the reports folder: Bob can view the Q3 report, and nothing changes"),
    expect(Request.Share(ann, Target.Doc(plan), Grantee.Person(bob), Level.View, None), at(library), Answer.Done,
      at(bobViewsPlan), "Ann shares the plan with Bob: the store holds the new share"),
    expect(Request.Share(bob, Target.Doc(plan), Grantee.Person(bob), Level.Edit, None), at(library), Answer.Refused,
      at(library), "Bob may not edit the plan: refused, and the store keeps the library"),
    reject(Request.Share(ann, Target.Doc(plan), Grantee.Person(bob), Level.View, None), at(library), Answer.Done,
      at(library), "a change answered done is kept"),
    reject(Request.Access(cat, plan), at(library), Answer.Access(Some(Level.View)), at(library),
      "Cat has no access to the plan"))

handleContract = fun (r : Request) => do
    let t ← Clock.now
    let lib ← LibraryStore.load
    if ((⟦SharingHttp.afterRequest⟧ lib t r) ≠ lib) then
      LibraryStore.save (⟦SharingHttp.afterRequest⟧ lib t r)
      pure ()
    else
      pure ()
    pure (⟦SharingHttp.answerTo⟧ lib t r)

the library in memory or in a SQLite file. Versions, deny rules, audit logs and
outside identity providers are not part of it yet.

      .on[Request.Share]((by, what, _, _, _) => allowedWhen(mayEdit(lib, t, by, what)))
      .on[Request.Unshare]((by, what, _) => allowedWhen(mayEdit(lib, t, by, what)))
      .on[Request.Move]((by, d, into) => allowedWhen(Sharing.mayMove(lib, t, by, d, into)))
      .on[Request.Invite]((by, _, what, _) => allowedWhen(mayEdit(lib, t, by, what)))
      .on[Request.Accept]((p, what) => allowedWhen(lib.invitations.exists(i => i.to === p && i.what === what && isOpen(i, t))))
      .on[Request.Withdraw]((by, _, what) => allowedWhen(mayEdit(lib, t, by, what)))
      .on[Request.Trash]((by, d) => allowedWhen(mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d))))

val handleContract = Node.contract(handle)("HandleContract",
  "A request is answered at the time the clock gives, from the library the store holds, and leaves the store holding the library it leads to: a question is answered with the person's access and changes nothing; a change is made as its operation makes it, and answered done when it may be made and refused otherwise. Handling does not move the clock.",
  why = "This is the service as a client sees it, in the store's and the clock's terms (LibraryKept, ClockKept). What the answers and changes are is the operations' (their contracts); what this adds is that each request reads the library the last one left and the clock once, and leaves the library it leads to, so a client's next request sees its change.",
  idea = "Serving"
)((r, result, before, after) =>
  after(LibraryModel) === afterRequest(before(LibraryModel), before(ClockModel).now, r) && after(ClockModel) === before(ClockModel) &&
    result === answerTo(before(LibraryModel), before(ClockModel).now, r))
  .under(accessFollowsShares)
  .examples()(
    expect(Request.Access(bob, q3Report), at(library), Answer.Access(Some(Level.View)), at(library),
      "Bob's team may view the reports folder: Bob can view the Q3 report, and nothing changes"),
    expect(Request.Share(ann, Target.Doc(plan), Grantee.Person(bob), Level.View, None), at(library), Answer.Done,
      at(bobViewsPlan), "Ann shares the plan with Bob: the store holds the new share"),
    expect(Request.Share(bob, Target.Doc(plan), Grantee.Person(bob), Level.Edit, None), at(library), Answer.Refused,
      at(library), "Bob may not edit the plan: refused, and the store keeps the library"),
    reject(Request.Share(ann, Target.Doc(plan), Grantee.Person(bob), Level.View, None), at(library), Answer.Done,
      at(library), "a change answered done is kept"),
    reject(Request.Access(cat, plan), at(library), Answer.Access(Some(Level.View)), at(library),
      "Cat has no access to the plan"))

forall((pre: Term[List[Event]], post: Term[List[Event]]) => forall((e: Term[Event]) =>
    (events === pre ++ (e :: post)) ==>
      e.on[Event.Asked](_ => True).on[Event.Housekept.type](True)
        .on[Event.Waited](d => after(pre).now + d <= after(pre).tidied + housekeepingWithin)))

vocabulary: events: what has happened to the service since it started, in order: the requests answered, the runs of housekeeping, and time passing
gone: whether a document is gone at a moment: past restoring, purged by the next housekeeping
housekeepingWithin: the longest the service goes without a run of housekeeping, in seconds
inForce: whether a share is in force at a moment: it gives access then
isOpen: whether an invitation is open at a moment: it can be accepted then
mayEdit: whether a person may edit a document or folder at a moment
startedAt: when the service started, in seconds

case class Invitation(to: PersonId, what: Target, level: Level, by: PersonId, sent: BigInt)
case class Library(documents: List[Document], folders: List[Folder], teams: List[Team], shares: List[Share], invitations: List[Invitation])
case class Moment(library: Library, now: BigInt, tidied: BigInt)

Run.after = (es: Term[List[Event]]) =>
    es.foldLeft(Moment(Library(Nil, Nil, Nil, Nil, Nil), startedAt, startedAt): Term[Moment])((m, e) => step(m, e))

Run.step = (m: Term[Moment], e: Term[Event]) =>
    e.on[Event.Asked](r => m.copy((library = answered(m.library, m.now, r))))
      .on[Event.Housekept.type](m.copy((library = Housekeeping.tidyCode(m.library, m.now), tidied = m.now)))
      .on[Event.Waited](d => m.copy((now = m.now + d)))

Run.answered = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], r: Term[Request]) =>
    r.on[Request.Access]((_, _) => lib)
      .on[Request.Share]((by, what, withWhom, level, until) => Sharing.shareCode(lib, t, by, Share(what, withWhom, level, until)))
      .on[Request.Unshare]((by, what, withWhom) => Sharing.unshareCode(lib, t, by, what, withWhom))
      .on[Request.Move]((by, d, into) => Sharing.moveCode(lib, t, by, d, into))
      .on[Request.Invite]((by, to, what, level) => Invitations.inviteCode(lib, t, by, to, what, level))
      .on[Request.Accept]((p, what) => Invitations.acceptCode(lib, t, p, what))
      .on[Request.Withdraw]((by, to, what) => Invitations.withdrawCode(lib, t, by, to, what))
      .on[Request.Trash]((by, d) => Trash.trashCode(lib, t, by, d))
      .on[Request.Restore]((by, d) => Trash.restoreCode(lib, t, by, d))

Sharing.shareCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], s: Term[Share]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, s.what).fold(lib.copy((shares = s :: sharesWithout(lib.shares, s.what, s.withWhom))), lib)

Sharing.sharesWithout = (ss: Term[List[Share]], what: Term[Target], withWhom: Term[Grantee]) =>
    ss.filterNot(s => s.what === what && s.withWhom === withWhom)

Sharing.unshareCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target], withWhom: Term[Grantee]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((shares = sharesWithout(lib.shares, what, withWhom))), lib)

Sharing.moveCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    val placed = foldersAt(lib, into)
    mayMove(lib, t, by, d, into).fold(lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d).fold(doc.copy((folders = placed)), doc)))), lib)

Sharing.mayMove = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)) &&
      into.fold(True)(f => lib.folders.exists(folder => folder.id === f) && mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.InFolder](f)))

Sharing.foldersAt = (lib: Term[Library], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    into.fold(List.empty[FolderId])(f => lib.folders.find(folder => folder.id === f).fold(List.empty[FolderId])(folder => folder.folders ++ List(f)))

Invitations.inviteCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target], level: Term[Level]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((invitations = Invitation(to, what, level, by, t) :: invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, to, what))), lib)

Invitations.invitationsWithout = (is: Term[List[Invitation]], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    is.filterNot(i => i.to === to && i.what === what)

Invitations.acceptCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], p: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    lib.invitations.find(i => i.to === p && i.what === what && isOpen(i, t)).fold(lib)(i =>
      lib.copy((shares = Share(what, Grantee[Grantee.Person](p), i.level, none[BigInt]) :: sharesWithout(lib.shares, what, Grantee[Grantee.Person](p)),
        invitations = invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, p, what))))

Invitations.withdrawCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((invitations = invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, to, what))), lib)

Trash.trashCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)).fold(
      lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d && !doc.trashed.isDefined).fold(doc.copy((trashed = some(t))), doc)))), lib)

Trash.restoreCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayRestore(lib, t, by, d).fold(
      lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d && !gone(doc, t)).fold(doc.copy((trashed = none[BigInt])), doc)))), lib)

Trash.mayRestore = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)) && lib.documents.exists(doc => doc.id === d && doc.trashed.isDefined && !gone(doc, t))

Housekeeping.tidyCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt]) =>
    lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.filterNot(doc => gone(doc, t)),
      shares = lib.shares.filter(s => inForce(s, t) && !ofGone(lib, t, s)),
      invitations = lib.invitations.filter(i => isOpen(i, t))))

Housekeeping.ofGone = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], s: Term[Share]) =>
    lib.documents.exists(doc => gone(doc, t) && s.what === Target[Target.Doc](doc.id))

val housekeepingOnTime = Node.assumption("HousekeepingOnTime",
  "Housekeeping runs often enough: time never moves on more than two minutes past its last run.",
  why = "The scheduler starts housekeeping every minute (Housekeeping.schedule); this is what the deadlines need of it. Not proven: the server checks it as it runs, and the tests show which claims fail without it.",
  idea = "Time and housekeeping"
)(forall((pre: Term[List[Event]], post: Term[List[Event]]) => forall((e: Term[Event]) =>
  (events === pre ++ (e :: post)) ==>
    e.on[Event.Asked](_ => True).on[Event.Housekept.type](True)
      .on[Event.Waited](d => after(pre).now + d <= after(pre).tidied + housekeepingWithin))))
  .under(Deadlines.trashPurgedOnTime, Deadlines.invitationsLapseOnTime)
content.idea:
## Time and housekeeping

Time is the server's clock, in seconds, read once for each request: a request
is answered at one moment. Housekeeping runs every minute, one at a time with
the requests; it removes shares that have ended, invitations that have lapsed,
and documents gone from the trash. Nothing waits for it: it only tidies.

content.idea:
# Sharing documents

People keep documents in folders and share them with other people, or with
teams. The shares decide who can view a document and who can edit it, and who
may change whom it is shared with.

From: Q1, Q5

## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share reaches them and
covers it, and edit it exactly when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is.

The service answers these questions and makes these changes over HTTP, keeping
the library in memory or in a SQLite file. Versions, deny rules, expiring
shares, audit logs and outside identity providers are not part of it yet.

From: Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5

content.idea:
# Sharing documents

People keep documents in folders and share them with other people, or with
teams. The shares decide who can view a document and who can edit it, and who
may change whom it is shared with. Shares can end, invitations lapse, and
documents in the trash are deleted for good after a while.

From: Q1, Q5

## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share in force reaches
them and covers it and the document is not in the trash, and edit it exactly
when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is. Moving a document out of a folder may take away the mover's own
access, and the last edit share of a document may be unshared.

From: Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q10, Q11

## Expiring shares

A share may be given until a time. From that time on it gives no access,
whether or not housekeeping has removed it yet: access is worked out from the
clock when it is asked. Sharing again replaces the end time.

From: Q6

## Invitations

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can invite a person to it, at a level,
and withdraw the invitation. An invitation gives no access until the person
accepts it; accepting it makes the share. An invitation can be accepted for 7
days after it is sent; then it lapses, and housekeeping removes it.

From: Q7

## Trash

Deleting a document puts it in the trash, where it gives nobody access, whatever
its shares. Anyone who can edit it can restore it for 30 days, and its shares
hold again. After 30 days it is gone: it can no longer be restored, and
housekeeping deletes it and its shares for good, never before.

From: Q8

## Time and housekeeping

Time is the server's clock, in seconds, read once for each request: a request
is answered at one moment. Housekeeping runs every minute, one at a time with
the requests; it removes shares that have ended, invitations that have lapsed,
and documents gone from the trash. Nothing waits for it: it only tidies.

From: Q9

## Serving

The service answers these questions and makes these changes over HTTP, keeping
the library in memory or in a SQLite file. Versions, deny rules, audit logs and
outside identity providers are not part of it yet.

From: Q5

enum Request: case Access(person: PersonId, doc: DocumentId), case Share(by: PersonId, what: Target, withWhom: Grantee, level: Level, until: Option[BigInt]), case Unshare(by: PersonId, what: Target, withWhom: Grantee), case Move(by: PersonId, doc: DocumentId, into: Option[FolderId]), case Invite(by: PersonId, to: PersonId, what: Target, level: Level), case Accept(person: PersonId, what: Target), case Withdraw(by: PersonId, to: PersonId, what: Target), case Trash(by: PersonId, doc: DocumentId), case Restore(by: PersonId, doc: DocumentId)

      .on[Event.Housekept.type](m.copy((library = Housekeeping.tidyCode(m.library, m.now), tidied = m.now)))
      .on[Event.Waited](d => m.copy((now = m.now + d)))

      .on[Request.Share]((by, what, withWhom, level, until) => Sharing.shareCode(lib, t, by, Share(what, withWhom, level, until)))
      .on[Request.Unshare]((by, what, withWhom) => Sharing.unshareCode(lib, t, by, what, withWhom))
      .on[Request.Move]((by, d, into) => Sharing.moveCode(lib, t, by, d, into))
      .on[Request.Invite]((by, to, what, level) => Invitations.inviteCode(lib, t, by, to, what, level))
      .on[Request.Accept]((p, what) => Invitations.acceptCode(lib, t, p, what))
      .on[Request.Withdraw]((by, to, what) => Invitations.withdrawCode(lib, t, by, to, what))
      .on[Request.Trash]((by, d) => Trash.trashCode(lib, t, by, d))
      .on[Request.Restore]((by, d) => Trash.restoreCode(lib, t, by, d))

Sharing.shareCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], s: Term[Share]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, s.what).fold(lib.copy((shares = s :: sharesWithout(lib.shares, s.what, s.withWhom))), lib)

Sharing.sharesWithout = (ss: Term[List[Share]], what: Term[Target], withWhom: Term[Grantee]) =>
    ss.filterNot(s => s.what === what && s.withWhom === withWhom)

Sharing.unshareCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target], withWhom: Term[Grantee]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((shares = sharesWithout(lib.shares, what, withWhom))), lib)

Sharing.moveCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    val placed = foldersAt(lib, into)
    mayMove(lib, t, by, d, into).fold(lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d).fold(doc.copy((folders = placed)), doc)))), lib)

Sharing.mayMove = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)) &&
      into.fold(True)(f => lib.folders.exists(folder => folder.id === f) && mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.InFolder](f)))

Sharing.foldersAt = (lib: Term[Library], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    into.fold(List.empty[FolderId])(f => lib.folders.find(folder => folder.id === f).fold(List.empty[FolderId])(folder => folder.folders ++ List(f)))

Invitations.inviteCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target], level: Term[Level]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((invitations = Invitation(to, what, level, by, t) :: invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, to, what))), lib)

Invitations.invitationsWithout = (is: Term[List[Invitation]], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    is.filterNot(i => i.to === to && i.what === what)

Invitations.acceptCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], p: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    lib.invitations.find(i => i.to === p && i.what === what && isOpen(i, t)).fold(lib)(i =>
      lib.copy((shares = Share(what, Grantee[Grantee.Person](p), i.level, none[BigInt]) :: sharesWithout(lib.shares, what, Grantee[Grantee.Person](p)),
        invitations = invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, p, what))))

Invitations.withdrawCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((invitations = invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, to, what))), lib)

Trash.trashCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)).fold(
      lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d && !doc.trashed.isDefined).fold(doc.copy((trashed = some(t))), doc)))), lib)

Trash.restoreCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayRestore(lib, t, by, d).fold(
      lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d && !gone(doc, t)).fold(doc.copy((trashed = none[BigInt])), doc)))), lib)

Trash.mayRestore = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)) && lib.documents.exists(doc => doc.id === d && doc.trashed.isDefined && !gone(doc, t))

Housekeeping.tidyCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt]) =>
    lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.filterNot(doc => gone(doc, t)),
      shares = lib.shares.filter(s => inForce(s, t) && !ofGone(lib, t, s)),
      invitations = lib.invitations.filter(i => isOpen(i, t))))

Housekeeping.ofGone = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], s: Term[Share]) =>
    lib.documents.exists(doc => gone(doc, t) && s.what === Target[Target.Doc](doc.id))

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share reaches them and
covers it, and edit it exactly when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is.

The service answers these questions and makes these changes over HTTP, keeping
the library in memory or in a SQLite file. Versions, deny rules, expiring
shares, audit logs and outside identity providers are not part of it yet.

val moveContract = Node.contract(move)("MoveContract",
  "Someone who may edit a document moves it into a folder they may edit, or out of every folder: the document is then in that folder and in every folder around it. When anyone else asks, or the folder does not exist, nothing changes.",
  why = "Moving a document changes who may see it, through the folders' shares (Cover), so it needs the right to edit both the document and the folder it goes into.",
  idea = "Who can see and change what"
)((lib, by, d, into, result) =>
  result === mayMove(lib, by, d, into).fold(
    lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d).fold(doc.copy((folders = foldersAt(lib, into))), doc)))),
    lib))
  .under(accessFollowsShares)
  .examples()(
    expect(library, ann, plan, Some(reports),
      library.copy(documents = List(Document(plan, "Plan", List(reports)), Document(q3Report, "Q3 report", List(reports, q3)))),
      "Ann may edit the plan and the reports folder: the plan moves into it"),
    expect(library, bob, q3Report, None, library, "Bob may only view the Q3 report: it stays where it is"),
    reject(library, ann, plan, Some(FolderId("nowhere")),
      library.copy(documents = List(Document(plan, "Plan", List(FolderId("nowhere"))), Document(q3Report, "Q3 report", List(reports, q3)))),

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share reaches them and
covers it, and edit it exactly when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is.

The service answers these questions and makes these changes over HTTP, keeping
the library in memory or in a SQLite file. Versions, deny rules, expiring
shares, audit logs and outside identity providers are not part of it yet.

## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share in force reaches
them and covers it and the document is not in the trash, and edit it exactly
when such a share is an edit share.

it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a

content.idea:
## Trash

Deleting a document puts it in the trash, where it gives nobody access, whatever
its shares. Anyone who can edit it can restore it for 30 days, and its shares
hold again. After 30 days it is gone: it can no longer be restored, and
housekeeping deletes it and its shares for good, never before.

ServerWiring.reason: Routes, codes, pool, time limits and 500s as decided for the HTTP layer; the codec is tested and the server checked against an oracle.

content.statement: The server reads each HTTP request into a request (an unreadable one is answered 400 with its reason, an unknown route 404), answers it with HandleContract's flow on the store, one request at a time, and writes the answer as JSON (a refused change is 403); requests run on a pool of workers with a time limit each (503 past it), and an internal error is answered 500 and logged.
content.why: What a request is answered with, and what it leaves in the store, is proven (HandleContract). Reading HTTP, the routes, the threads and the time limits are decided here and reviewed; the reading and writing of HTTP is tested against the routes this states (SharingSuite). One request at a time makes each read the library the last one left, which HandleContract assumes. SharingService, Sharing's methods as plain Scala, runs the same proven code.

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share reaches them and
covers it, and edit it exactly when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is.

The service answers these questions and makes these changes over HTTP, keeping
the library in memory or in a SQLite file. Versions, deny rules, expiring
shares, audit logs and outside identity providers are not part of it yet.

val shareContract = Node.contract(share)("ShareContract",
  "Someone who may edit a document or folder shares it with a person or a team at a level, for good or until a time: the new share takes the place of any earlier share of it with them. When anyone else asks, nothing changes.",
  why = "Anyone who can edit a document can share it (Q2), and a person or team has one share of a thing at a time, so sharing again changes the level and the end rather than adding a second share (Q6).",
  idea = "Who can see and change what"
)((lib, t, by, s, result) =>
  result === mayEdit(lib, t, by, s.what).fold(lib.copy((shares = s :: sharesWithout(lib.shares, s.what, s.withWhom))), lib))
  .under(accessFollowsShares)
  .examples()(
    expect(library, now, ann, bobViewsPlan, library.copy(shares = bobViewsPlan :: library.shares),
      "Ann may edit the plan, so she shares it with Bob"),
    expect(library, now, ann, bobViewsPlanForAnHour, library.copy(shares = bobViewsPlanForAnHour :: library.shares),
      "Ann shares the plan with Bob for an hour"),
    expect(library, now, bob, Share(Target.Doc(plan), Grantee.Person(bob), Level.Edit, None), library,
      "Bob may not edit the plan: his request changes nothing"),
    reject(library, now, bob, catViewsReports, library.copy(shares = catViewsReports :: library.shares),
      "Bob may only view the reports folder, so he cannot share it"))

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share in force reaches
them and covers it and the document is not in the trash, and edit it exactly
when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is. Moving a document out of a folder may take away the mover's own
access, and the last edit share of a document may be unshared.

content.why: Q6–Q8: ended shares and lapsed invitations give nothing and are removed; a document 30 days in the trash is deleted for good, with its shares (Q8), so they cannot come back to anything. The folders and teams are not touched.

  "Tidying at a moment keeps the shares in force, except those of a document gone; keeps the invitations still open; and keeps the documents not gone. Everything else stays as it was.",
  why = "Q6–Q8: ended shares and lapsed invitations give nothing and are removed; a document 30 days in the trash is deleted for good, with its shares (Q8), so they cannot come back to anything. The folders and teams are not touched.",

    shares = lib.shares.filter(s => inForce(s, t) && !ofGone(lib, t, s)),
    invitations = lib.invitations.filter(i => isOpen(i, t)))))

content.idea:
## Time and housekeeping

Time is the server's clock, in seconds, read once for each request: a request
is answered at one moment. Housekeeping runs every minute, one at a time with
the requests; it removes shares that have ended, invitations that have lapsed,
and documents gone from the trash. Nothing waits for it: it only tidies.

TrashContract.reason: Q8: deleting is putting in the trash, by editors; a second delete keeps the first time.

content.statement: Someone who may edit a document puts it in the trash: it is in the trash from now on, unless it was already, when it keeps the time it was put there. When anyone else asks, nothing changes.
content.why: Q8: deleting a document puts it in the trash for a while rather than deleting it for good. Deleting is a change to the document, so only someone who may edit it does it.

  "Someone who may edit a document puts it in the trash: it is in the trash from now on, unless it was already, when it keeps the time it was put there. When anyone else asks, nothing changes.",
  why = "Q8: deleting a document puts it in the trash for a while rather than deleting it for good. Deleting is a change to the document, so only someone who may edit it does it.",
  idea = "Trash"
)((lib, t, by, d, result) =>
  result === mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)).fold(
    lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d && !doc.trashed.isDefined).fold(doc.copy((trashed = some(t))), doc)))), lib))
  .under(accessFollowsShares)
  .examples()(
    expect(library, now - day, ann, plan, planInTrash, "Ann may edit the plan: it goes to the trash"),
    expect(planInTrash, now, ann, plan, planInTrash, "already in the trash: it keeps its time"),
    expect(library, now, bob, plan, library, "Bob may not edit the plan"),
    reject(library, now, bob, q3Report, library.copy(documents = List(planDoc, q3ReportDoc.copy(trashed = Some(now)))),
      "Bob may only view the Q3 report: he cannot delete it"))

content.idea:
## Trash

Deleting a document puts it in the trash, where it gives nobody access, whatever
its shares. Anyone who can edit it can restore it for 30 days, and its shares
hold again. After 30 days it is gone: it can no longer be restored, and
housekeeping deletes it and its shares for good, never before.

TrashLifetime.reason: Q8: the trash keeps a document for 30 days.

content.statement: A document stays in the trash for 30 days.
content.why: Q8: a document in the trash can be restored for 30 days, then it is deleted for good.
vocabulary: trashKeeps: how long a document stays in the trash before it is gone, in seconds

TrashPurgedOnTime.reason: Q8: never before 30 days (each run) and within 30 days and the housekeeping bound (every run that keeps HousekeepingOnTime).

content.statement: A document in the trash is purged after 30 days and never before: housekeeping removes only documents 30 days in the trash, and while it runs at least every two minutes no document stays in the trash longer than 30 days and two minutes.
content.why: Q8, as a safety (never before: each run of housekeeping) and a bounded response (after: every moment the service reaches, given the scheduler's period, HousekeepingOnTime). Unbounded "eventually purged" is weaker and could not be tested.

sources.formula:
forall((lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt]) =>
    lib.documents.forall(doc => Housekeeping.tidyCode(lib, t).documents.contains(doc) || doc.trashed.fold(False)(at => at + trashKeeps <= t))) &&
    after(events).library.documents.forall(doc => doc.trashed.fold(True)(at => after(events).now < at + trashKeeps + housekeepingWithin))

vocabulary: events: what has happened to the service since it started, in order: the requests answered, the runs of housekeeping, and time passing
gone: whether a document is gone at a moment: past restoring, purged by the next housekeeping
housekeepingWithin: the longest the service goes without a run of housekeeping, in seconds
inForce: whether a share is in force at a moment: it gives access then
isOpen: whether an invitation is open at a moment: it can be accepted then
mayEdit: whether a person may edit a document or folder at a moment
startedAt: when the service started, in seconds
trashKeeps: how long a document stays in the trash before it is gone, in seconds
uses: case class DocumentId(name: String)
case class FolderId(name: String)
case class Document(id: DocumentId, title: String, folders: List[FolderId], trashed: Option[BigInt])
case class Folder(id: FolderId, name: String, folders: List[FolderId])
case class TeamId(name: String)
case class PersonId(name: String)
case class Team(id: TeamId, members: List[PersonId])
enum Target: case Doc(id: DocumentId), case InFolder(id: FolderId)
enum Grantee: case Person(id: PersonId), case Team(id: TeamId)
enum Level: case View, case Edit
case class Share(what: Target, withWhom: Grantee, level: Level, until: Option[BigInt])
case class Invitation(to: PersonId, what: Target, level: Level, by: PersonId, sent: BigInt)
case class Library(documents: List[Document], folders: List[Folder], teams: List[Team], shares: List[Share], invitations: List[Invitation])
case class Moment(library: Library, now: BigInt, tidied: BigInt)

enum Request: case Access(person: PersonId, doc: DocumentId), case Share(by: PersonId, what: Target, withWhom: Grantee, level: Level, until: Option[BigInt]), case Unshare(by: PersonId, what: Target, withWhom: Grantee), case Move(by: PersonId, doc: DocumentId, into: Option[FolderId]), case Invite(by: PersonId, to: PersonId, what: Target, level: Level), case Accept(person: PersonId, what: Target), case Withdraw(by: PersonId, to: PersonId, what: Target), case Trash(by: PersonId, doc: DocumentId), case Restore(by: PersonId, doc: DocumentId)
enum Event: case Asked(request: Request), case Housekept, case Waited(seconds: BigInt)

Housekeeping.tidyCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt]) =>
    lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.filterNot(doc => gone(doc, t)),
      shares = lib.shares.filter(s => inForce(s, t) && !ofGone(lib, t, s)),
      invitations = lib.invitations.filter(i => isOpen(i, t))))

Housekeeping.ofGone = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], s: Term[Share]) =>
    lib.documents.exists(doc => gone(doc, t) && s.what === Target[Target.Doc](doc.id))

Run.after = (es: Term[List[Event]]) =>
    es.foldLeft(Moment(Library(Nil, Nil, Nil, Nil, Nil), startedAt, startedAt): Term[Moment])((m, e) => step(m, e))

Run.step = (m: Term[Moment], e: Term[Event]) =>
    e.on[Event.Asked](r => m.copy((library = answered(m.library, m.now, r))))
      .on[Event.Housekept.type](m.copy((library = Housekeeping.tidyCode(m.library, m.now), tidied = m.now)))
      .on[Event.Waited](d => m.copy((now = m.now + d)))

Run.answered = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], r: Term[Request]) =>
    r.on[Request.Access]((_, _) => lib)
      .on[Request.Share]((by, what, withWhom, level, until) => Sharing.shareCode(lib, t, by, Share(what, withWhom, level, until)))
      .on[Request.Unshare]((by, what, withWhom) => Sharing.unshareCode(lib, t, by, what, withWhom))
      .on[Request.Move]((by, d, into) => Sharing.moveCode(lib, t, by, d, into))
      .on[Request.Invite]((by, to, what, level) => Invitations.inviteCode(lib, t, by, to, what, level))
      .on[Request.Accept]((p, what) => Invitations.acceptCode(lib, t, p, what))
      .on[Request.Withdraw]((by, to, what) => Invitations.withdrawCode(lib, t, by, to, what))
      .on[Request.Trash]((by, d) => Trash.trashCode(lib, t, by, d))
      .on[Request.Restore]((by, d) => Trash.restoreCode(lib, t, by, d))

Sharing.shareCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], s: Term[Share]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, s.what).fold(lib.copy((shares = s :: sharesWithout(lib.shares, s.what, s.withWhom))), lib)

Sharing.sharesWithout = (ss: Term[List[Share]], what: Term[Target], withWhom: Term[Grantee]) =>
    ss.filterNot(s => s.what === what && s.withWhom === withWhom)

Sharing.unshareCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target], withWhom: Term[Grantee]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((shares = sharesWithout(lib.shares, what, withWhom))), lib)

Sharing.moveCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    val placed = foldersAt(lib, into)
    mayMove(lib, t, by, d, into).fold(lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d).fold(doc.copy((folders = placed)), doc)))), lib)

Sharing.mayMove = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)) &&
      into.fold(True)(f => lib.folders.exists(folder => folder.id === f) && mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.InFolder](f)))

Sharing.foldersAt = (lib: Term[Library], into: Term[Option[FolderId]]) =>
    into.fold(List.empty[FolderId])(f => lib.folders.find(folder => folder.id === f).fold(List.empty[FolderId])(folder => folder.folders ++ List(f)))

Invitations.inviteCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target], level: Term[Level]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((invitations = Invitation(to, what, level, by, t) :: invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, to, what))), lib)

Invitations.invitationsWithout = (is: Term[List[Invitation]], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    is.filterNot(i => i.to === to && i.what === what)

Invitations.acceptCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], p: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    lib.invitations.find(i => i.to === p && i.what === what && isOpen(i, t)).fold(lib)(i =>
      lib.copy((shares = Share(what, Grantee[Grantee.Person](p), i.level, none[BigInt]) :: sharesWithout(lib.shares, what, Grantee[Grantee.Person](p)),
        invitations = invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, p, what))))

Invitations.withdrawCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], to: Term[PersonId], what: Term[Target]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((invitations = invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, to, what))), lib)

Trash.trashCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)).fold(
      lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d && !doc.trashed.isDefined).fold(doc.copy((trashed = some(t))), doc)))), lib)

Trash.restoreCode = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayRestore(lib, t, by, d).fold(
      lib.copy((documents = lib.documents.map(doc => (doc.id === d && !gone(doc, t)).fold(doc.copy((trashed = none[BigInt])), doc)))), lib)

Trash.mayRestore = (lib: Term[Library], t: Term[BigInt], by: Term[PersonId], d: Term[DocumentId]) =>
    mayEdit(lib, t, by, Target[Target.Doc](d)) && lib.documents.exists(doc => doc.id === d && doc.trashed.isDefined && !gone(doc, t))

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share reaches them and
covers it, and edit it exactly when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is.

The service answers these questions and makes these changes over HTTP, keeping
the library in memory or in a SQLite file. Versions, deny rules, expiring
shares, audit logs and outside identity providers are not part of it yet.

content.idea:
## Who can see and change what

A person can view or edit a document; being able to edit it includes being able
to view it. A share gives one person, or everyone in one team, view or edit on
one document, or on a folder and everything inside it, at any depth. Teams
contain people only. Folders form a tree, and a document is in at most one
folder. A person can view a document exactly when some share in force reaches
them and covers it and the document is not in the trash, and edit it exactly
when such a share is an edit share.

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can share it, or unshare it; sharing
it again with the same person or team changes the level. Moving a document into
a folder needs edit on both. Nobody else changes the shares, or where a
document is. Moving a document out of a folder may take away the mover's own
access, and the last edit share of a document may be unshared.

val withdrawContract = Node.contract(withdraw)("WithdrawContract",
  "Someone who may edit a document or folder withdraws a person's invitation to it: the invitation goes. When anyone else asks, nothing changes.",
  why = "Q7: an editor can take an offer back before it is accepted.",
  idea = "Invitations"
)((lib, t, by, to, what, result) =>
  result === mayEdit(lib, t, by, what).fold(lib.copy((invitations = invitationsWithout(lib.invitations, to, what))), lib))
  .under(accessFollowsShares)
  .examples()(
    expect(withCat, now, ann, cat, Target.Doc(plan), library, "Ann withdraws Cat's invitation"),
    expect(withCat, now, bob, cat, Target.Doc(plan), withCat, "Bob may not edit the plan: the invitation stays"),
    reject(withCat, now, bob, cat, Target.Doc(plan), library, "only an editor withdraws an invitation"))

content.idea:
## Invitations

Anyone who can edit a document or folder can invite a person to it, at a level,
and withdraw the invitation. An invitation gives no access until the person
accepts it; accepting it makes the share. An invitation can be accepted for 7
days after it is sent; then it lapses, and housekeeping removes it.
